title: SEC press releases and Form D notices tie a relative with a longer first name (Paula for Paul) to the person as confirmed
scenario: Subject Paul Lowell, company Lowell Robotics. The SEC press release 'SEC Charges Paula Lowell, CEO of Lowell Robotics' comes back confirmed with severity medium, which puts it under red flags. The company's Form D listing Paula Lowell as CEO also comes back confirmed, and a CEO role anchor is added for him. The cause is namesAgree with nickname:true, which accepts any 3-letter prefix (Eric/Erica, Dan/Daniela). matchText then puts subject.name into the text.
evidence: Temporary jest test through secPersonConnector.run with 'press' and 'formd'. Both findings were confirmed ('names Lowell Robotics'). subject.anchors.roles gained Lowell Robotics Inc as ceo from 2021-06-17.
fix: Drop the startsWith rule in namesAgree. Allow only real diminutives from the shared names.js table (personNameVariants or nameMatcher). In readPress, personPress, subjectOnFormD and buildComplaint, never put subject.name into matchText unless subject.hasName(listed name) is true. Otherwise hold the record at possible, with no role anchor and no noteCik.
verifyNote: Reproduced. 'SEC Charges Paula Lowell, CEO of Lowell Robotics' for subject Paul Lowell came back confirmed at medium severity. The cause is namesAgree line 132, where nickname:true accepts any 3-letter prefix, and readPress, which puts subject.name into matchText.
betterFix: Replace the startsWith rule with the shared diminutive table (personNameVariants or nameMatcher), so Sam/Samuel passes and Paula/Paul does not. When the listed name is only a nickname variant and not subject.hasName(listed), leave subject.name out of matchText and hold the record at likely or possible, with no noteCik and no role anchor. Add a Paula/Paul and an Erica/Eric test.

title: PRIVATE_MATTER, now applied to every court path, drops the company's own class action, Visa cases, custody firms and agency bans
scenario: A company check on Nikola Corporation. CourtListener returns 'In re Nikola Corporation Securities Litigation', whose party list includes 'Estate of John Q Investor', plus 'Nikola Corp. v. Visa U.S.A. Inc.' and a case against 'Anchorage Digital Custody LLC'. All three are dropped as private, and the note says they concern health or minors. The same regex also drops FDA debarment and export-denial orders whose abstracts mention psychiatric billing or visa fraud.
evidence: Temporary test of courtDocketsConnector.run (company): only 'Nikola Corporation v. Lion Electric' was kept. PRIVATE_MATTER.test returned true for 'Visa U.S.A. Inc.', 'Coinbase Custody Trust Company', 'Real Estate of Texas LLC' and both FR abstracts.
fix: Test only the caption (never the full party list) for the company path and for parties other than the person. Remove 'visa' and 'custody' as bare words, or require a context such as 'child custody' or 'visa petition|immigrant visa'. Anchor 'estate of' to the start of a side. Skip PRIVATE_MATTER on Federal Register agency orders (debarment and denial orders are public sanctions).
verifyNote: Reproduced on the company path: only 'Nikola Corporation v. Lion Electric' was kept. The Visa case and the class action were dropped because captionText includes the full party list. PRIVATE_MATTER matches 'Visa U.S.A.', 'Digital Custody LLC', 'Real Estate of Texas' and 'Estate of John Q Investor'.
betterFix: In docketFinding, test only the case name and full caption, never the parties, and skip PRIVATE_MATTER entirely when personal is false (company path). In the regex, use 'child custody|custody of', 'visa (?:petition|application|denial|refusal)|immigrant visa', and '^\s*(?:in re )?estate of'. FR debarment orders are a separate, smaller issue: excluded() predates the repair.

title: OpenSanctions grades with its own rule: a variant-name hit, or an employer learned from other records, raises a list entry to likely
scenario: Subject Maria Garcia, company Acme Robotics. The entry 'Maria Garcia Lopez' (tier 3, an extra surname) has the reason 'Fraud in the sale of Acme Robotics securities', and comes back likely without 'verify identity'. Subject Jane Roe with a found (not given) anchor Brightwater Securities: the FINRA entry 'JANE ROE ... registered with Brightwater Securities' also comes back likely. The shared gradeListedPerson, which ASIC and debarment use, returns possible in both cases.
evidence: Temporary test of openSanctionsConnector.run (os.us-markets): likely ['names Brightwater Securities', 'held at likely'] and likely for Garcia Lopez. gradeListedPerson on the same input returned possible.
fix: Replace graded() for the subject case with sanctions.gradeListedPerson(subject, f, { tier: hit.tier, context: row.r, possibleTitle }), then cap at likely as asic.js does. Use screenNames(task, ctx) for the searched names. Add tests for the tier-3 case and the non-given anchor case.
verifyNote: The tier-3 half reproduced: 'Maria Garcia Lopez' (tier 3) came back likely ('names Acme Robotics'). gradeListedPerson returns possible for tier>=3. The found-anchor half did not reproduce in my test (JANE ROE with a found Brightwater anchor came back possible), but the grader still ignores tier and anchor origin.
betterFix: For the subject task in graded(), call sanctions.gradeListedPerson(subject, f, { tier: hit.tier, context: row.r, possibleTitle: `${f.title}: name match only, verify identity` }) and keep the capped() hold at likely. Pass the tier through findingFor, which already has hit.tier.

title: SEC enforcement and trading-suspension lookups that fail in part return no partial, so coverage shows them as answered
scenario: The administrative-proceedings list returns 500 while litigation releases answer empty. personEnforcement returns notes ['SEC administrative proceedings could not be searched this time.'] and no partial. report.js decides a source's status from partial and errors, so the source reads as 'no match'. In companyEvents, a failed trading-suspension search and a Form D surname pass over SURNAME_MAX_HITS are also dropped without a partial.
evidence: Temporary test: admin list 500 gave {n:0, notes:[...could not be searched...], partial: undefined}. companyEvents catch block (around line 2273) pushes only a note.
fix: Return partial: ['SEC administrative proceedings (did not answer)'] or the litigation-releases equivalent when one list is rejected. Do the same in companyEvents' catch ('SEC trading suspensions (did not answer)') and in personFormD when result.total > SURNAME_MAX_HITS ('Form D notices under the surname (too many to read)').
verifyNote: Reproduced: with the admin list at 500 and litigation empty, the result was {findings:[], notes:[...could not be searched...]} with no partial, so report.js counts the source as fully answered. A failed trading-suspension search in companyEvents' catch also adds only a note.
betterFix: Add partial: ['SEC administrative proceedings (did not answer)'] or the litigation-releases equivalent when one of the two settles rejected. Do the same in companyEvents' catch. The Form D surname pass over SURNAME_MAX_HITS is a deliberate supplementary pass after the exact-phrase search: a note is enough there, and marking it partial would over-flag.

title: OpenSanctions and FDA debarment search a company only under the typed name, not its learned legal names
scenario: The company is typed 'Ramp', and the check later learns the legal name 'Ramp Business Corporation'. OpenSanctions and FDA debarment screen only 'Ramp' (which stays possible because it is one word) and never the legal name. ASIC, FARA, the ESMA register and the sanctions screens use companyNames() and do search it, and FOUNDER-CHECK.md says every known name is searched.
fix: For company tasks, use screenNames(task, ctx) (sanctions.companyNames) in opensanctions.searchedNames and fdaDebarment.searchedNames. Grade a one-word name as possible only when the match came through the bare typed word, as asic.js does with `via`.
verifyNote: For a company task, opensanctions.js and fdaDebarment.js searchedNames return only [task.value]. asic.js uses screenNames(task, ctx), so a learned legal name is never screened by these two lists. Not reproduced at runtime, but clear in the code.
betterFix: For company tasks, use sanctions.screenNames(task, ctx) in both files. Keep the one-word grade at possible only when the hit came through the bare typed word, using a `via` flag as asic.js does.
